method: Artifact-first calibration against the current visual-media registry, the bound editorial reference, the final prose-bound contract, and the actual 1536 by 1024 still. Each STILL-applicable negative was considered as a failure condition before the admission judgment.

results.reason: A flat generic icon, glossy product shot, or unbound style would fail the adult editorial pop-art requirement. This calibration requires visible ink linework, halftone and print texture without reusing episode identity.
An invented named location, corporate logo, person, or unrelated workplace scene would exceed the conceptual desk brief and falsely locate the consultation.
A floating pen, unsupported lamp, detached cap, or impossible desk plane would fail the required coherent object supports and perspective.
Any visible person or malformed hand or body would fail. The final contract requires no people, so this still must remain people-free.
Any generated words, pseudo-text, logo, seal, checkmark, watermark, or fabricated document claim would breach the NO_VISIBLE_TEXT plan. Only simple horizontal rule marks are permitted.
Historical costume, dated technology, or an anachronistic period setting would create an unsupported era claim. The conceptual contemporary stationery scene must carry none.
A visual implying that rules are implemented, tested, guaranteed, approved, or already effective would contradict the story's proposed future conduct-code consultation.
Dominant decoration without a feedback or draft-writing job would fail object discipline. The sheet, pen and comment slips must remain the visual explanation.
